study.question: Can action-aware task-private history readouts add repeatable validation macro-AUC utility to g0 linear-moment joint representations beyond equal-parameter task-independent readouts, and does that utility depend on the signed position moment?
study.hypothesis: Observation: g0-r0005-linear_moment has macro AUC0.8283262734957326, macro Logloss0.054728202184133226, train365.04s, inference31.36s, and32948357 parameters; g3-r0004-click_score_stop has0.8123335254548857,0.05665085308601132,433.58s,32.48s,and32144072 parameters; DIN has0.8099233880793816. Every g0 task AUC exceeds g3, so standalone g3 performance does not establish complementarity. Inspection shows g0 shares one target relevance weighting and one joint token stack across tasks; g3 instead has private action-aware scorers and task-specific pooled histories, with the click scorer input detached. Proposed mechanism: a private action-aware direct history summary can preserve task-specific relevance that g0 shared token compression discards. Keep g0 token construction and one joint stack intact, add a task-private residual pooled summary to each tower direct global DIN summary. Four action-extended scorers retain the g3 private nonlinear architecture but have independent hidden initialization and zero output layers, preserving the parent initial function while avoiding a symmetric mean-control ensemble. This is a restricted compatibility test at the readout, not a full task-conditioned token stack or a replication of g3 initialization. Linear versus copy moments crosses position-sensitive representation with task-private versus averaged routing. No causal support or novelty is established.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the entire joint relation/temporal/moment representation and tower input dimensions. Add only four g3-style private relevance scorers as residuals in the direct history slot. The shared g0 scorer still supplies every joint token.

Inherit private nonlinear action-aware unnormalized scoring and label-specific scorer-input stops. Independent scalar outputs are equivalent to private trunks with separate output rows, but initialize private hidden weights independently with zero output layers instead of the g3 cloned-scorer initialization and retain g0 shared token representation. No whole-model g3 reproduction claim.

Primary archived section4.3 lines250-282 verifies target-conditioned unnormalized weighted history sums. Extend this inherited component with private feedback-task readouts and existing relation/moment token interaction; not an original attention claim.

Pinned benchmark forward lines123-170 uses task-mask-initialized sequence hubs and task tokens with stacked aggregation/broadcast. Here one shared g0 JointBlock remains and private target/action scorers feed only direct tower summaries. This is code inspection, not the unavailable original-paper audit.

Section2.3 describes INFNet hubs and EST cross-attention/field-specific FFNs. This proposal adds neither a hub broadcast stack nor field-specific FFNs. Original INFNet/EST/UniMixer text was unavailable or not inspected; original-method priority remains unverified.

study.proposed_difference: Four-cell crossed design: linear_private is the candidate; linear_mean, copy_private and copy_mean are controls. All allocate/execute four identical-shape action-extended scorers. private routes column t to tower t; mean broadcasts the arithmetic mean of all four columns, removing task-specific readout while retaining active scorer capacity. Each tower adds this routed residual to its existing112-dimensional global history slot (for released six16-d item fields plus action); no added tower width or token count. copy replaces signed within-bin moment coefficients by one on valid events, retaining a trainable duplicate of the ordinary relation sum at identical projection/compute shape. This removes only signed-position information, not the full relation representation. Mean versus private changes gradient mixing as well as routing; capacity equality alone does not eliminate that alternative. task_routing=parent is a diagnostic replay mode only, not a fifth proposed experiment. Gradient-stop flags remain executable for later matched follow-ups; this batch does not identify gradient isolation. Prospective design revision before execution: identical cloned private scorers in a mean ensemble can remain symmetric, making nominal parameter matching overstate effective capacity. Therefore all four residual scorers use distinct hidden initialization and zero scalar output layers in both routing arms. Initial residuals are zero; hidden networks become trainable after the output layer first updates. Mean control retains four distinct nonlinear basis functions; verify diversity/gradient activation on host. Earlier clone-and-replace design was abandoned before any numerical execution or training; source patch application initially failed atomically due to hunk order, then was corrected. All preparation cost counts; neither is scientific counterevidence.
predictions: At initialization, all four cells have numerically equal outputs to g0 linear source: moment projection and private residual output weights/biases are zero. Private hidden weights differ across branches, with identical complete initial states across factorial cells. Verify both output equality and branch diversity in eval and cloned-state train modes before training.

After training, linear_private exceeds BOTH frozen source validation macro AUCs and linear_mean on paired repeated seeds if private readout adds useful evidence beyond capacity. Report all four task AUC/Logloss deltas against g0, g3 and DIN, including regressions.

Estimate routing effects d_linear=AUC(linear_private)-AUC(linear_mean), d_copy=AUC(copy_private)-AUC(copy_mean), and interaction d_linear-d_copy. A positive interaction supports dependence on signed position information only if it repeats; positive routing effects with near-zero interaction suggest additive utility. A negative interaction indicates redundancy/interference, not automatically failure of either component.

falsifiers: No repeat-confirmed macro-AUC gain over g0 opposes utility of this readout implementation; it does not refute all combinations of the two source approaches.
Equal gains for mean routing oppose attribution to task-specific readout, even if both beat g0. No linear/copy interaction leaves a special synergy with signed moments unsupported.
Failure under matched source/seed replay, parameter audit, masking or gradient tests is an implementation/integrity failure; retain its costs and diagnose before interpreting performance.
No difference between block-click on/off or other available stop contrasts in later controlled trials leaves a gradient-isolation explanation unsupported. This batch supplies no such contrast.

alternative_explanations: Added active nonlinear scorer capacity or action-in-score features rather than task routing; mean routing controls these jointly but not changed gradient mixing.
Different initialization, BF16 reduction roundoff, Dice running statistics or dense AdamW effects; use identical source construction/RNG, audit initial equality and measured costs.

Shared embeddings couple the private branch back into g0 tokens; source-style stop only blocks a selected private scorer input, not all click gradients, and under mean routing that branch receives multiple task losses.
copy permits a second active projection of identical relation content and may optimize differently; it is a capacity-matched replacement, not an exact functional removal of parameters.
Single-epoch optimization, rare auxiliary label variance and offline action maturity assumptions; labels are user/category/brand24h outcomes, not advertisement-specific conversion attribution.

Only three committed observations are available. No failed or abandoned local trajectories or stop-factor comparisons were returned by scoped search, so no broader trajectory conclusion is justified. Do not import unseen parent outcomes from trial names.

Independent hidden initialization is needed for active capacity in mean routing, while zero residual outputs make trunk gradients zero on the first update. Verify nonzero output-layer gradients initially and nonzero hidden/action-column gradients after the first output update. This initialization differs from the committed g3 source and is not itself isolated here.

Mean versus private routing changes gradient dilution, pooled-summary variance and regularization in addition to loss-to-scorer connectivity. Equal parameter counts and forward shapes do not resolve these differences; follow-up normalization or loss-routing controls would be needed before a narrower explanation.
